classification.difficultyReason: Must question the existence of the requested angles rather than pursue an angle-sum formula, using positivity of the tangents and reciprocal bounds to expose contradictory givens.

content.prompt:
Given $0<\alpha,\beta,\gamma<\frac\pi2$ and
$$\begin{aligned}\tan\alpha+\tan\beta+\tan\gamma&=1\\\cot\alpha+\cot\beta+\cot\gamma&=1,\end{aligned}$$
find the value of $\alpha+\beta+\gamma$.

answer.short:
No such acute angles exist.

The tangent sum makes every tangent less than 1, so every cotangent exceeds 1, contradicting the cotangent sum.
answer.worked:
All three tangents are positive. Since their sum is 1,
$$0<\tan\alpha,\tan\beta,\tan\gamma<1.$$
Taking reciprocals,
$$\cot\alpha>1,\qquad\cot\beta>1,\qquad\cot\gamma>1.$$
Therefore
$$\cot\alpha+\cot\beta+\cot\gamma>3,$$
which contradicts the given sum of 1. No angles satisfy the printed conditions.
